工具测量每一帧相对基准帧的偏移，再以亚像素精度移回去。方法是相位相关：偏移表现为: The tool measures the offset of each frame relative to a base frame and moves it back with sub-pixel accuracy. The method is phase correlation: the offset is expressed as the phase difference between the spectra of the two images, so a Fourier transform per image can find an offset of two hundred pixels or two pixels at the same cost. Rotation and scaling are found in the logpolar spectrum in the same way. Automatically also measures areas distributed across the entire image, correcting perspective when enough reliable measurements agree. This helps the wide-angle starry sky stay aligned both at the edges and in the center. If additional corrections cannot be measured reliably, rotation and scaling are retained and no perspective correction is stated in the alignment details. The correction applies to the entire frame and cannot align independently moving objects, nor does it align all depths in a scene taken one step to the side. The frame shifted to the left cannot reach the right edge, so the result is cropped to the area covered by all the frames together, which may be slightly smaller. This avoids dark edges in uncovered areas.
